support: None of this needed to happen.
The council should put the first train back at dawn, load the cheese, and give the visitors the second train, which would still reach Gessen in good light for their photographs.
WV13-P01.6.note: The author faults the timetable change for abandoning the farmers and demands it be reversed, which is criticism, not longing, fear, admiration or amusement.

support: Putting a glass box on the sunny end of a west-facing terrace was the wrong decision, made for the sake of the café's takings.

exclusions.A: A class at Larch Street School had sent the council a careful scheme matching each bridge to a bus line, so that commuters could tell the bridges apart and find the right one, and it went into a drawer.
exclusions.C: Instead it has put a bright coat over eleven red rings and called the job finished.

support: What the bridges needed this summer was repair, not paint.
Instead it has put a bright coat over eleven red rings and called the job finished.
WV13-P03.5.note: The writer condemns painting over logged repairs and says what the city should have done instead; the dry remark about interviews sharpens the criticism rather than supporting amusement, and no fear for safety is voiced.

support: I typed my opening sentence and then sat for a long time turning the old repair tag from his shop over in my fingers.
Its ink has faded to the colour of weak tea.
WV13-P05.5.note: Lingering over the faded tag from a shop that has just closed shows longing for what is gone; gratitude appears elsewhere (March 9) but paragraph 4 signals loss, not thanks.
